references.text: Here the service age for the Levites is given as from 30 years, showing a variation in the age requirement for different aspects of Levitical service.
Repeats the age requirement of 30 years for the Levites' service at the tabernacle, which can be compared with the 25 years mentioned in 8:24.
Specifies the service age for the sons of Merari as 30 years, a parallel to the provisions regarding the Levites' years of service.
The continuation of the provision concerning the Levites' service, stating that they are to retire from service at the age of 50.
David counts the Levites from 30 years and upward, demonstrating the practical application of the age requirement for Levitical service.
David changes the service age to 20 years, explaining that the duties of the Levites have changed since the tabernacle now has a permanent dwelling place.
During Hezekiah's reign, the Levites are registered from the age of 20, showing the development of the age requirement throughout Israel's history.
At the rebuilding of the temple, the Levites are assigned to service from the age of 20, in accordance with David's later provision.
